paper.title: Neural Combinatorial Clustered Bandits for Recommendation Systems

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial bandit with semi-bandit feedback and neural (NTK) reward model
unmapped: super arm reward function u is unknown (no optimization oracle) and is learned by a monotone neural network; learner also observes super arm reward
context space assumed to have a clustered structure (Assumptions 5-6)
base arm reward h(x) in [0,1] Lipschitz in context (l1 norm)
settings.definition_quote: we consider a contextual combinatorial bandit with $N$ being the total number of arms and $T$ the total number of rounds. At the start of every round $t$, the agent observes the context vectors of all arms ... and chooses ... a super arm $S_t \subset [N]$ with a fixed size, or budget, $K$ ... r_{t,i} = h(x_{t,i}) + \xi_{t,i} ... where h is an unknown function satisfying 0 <= h(x) <= 1 and \xi_{t,i} is \zeta-sub-Gaussian noise

conditions: Assumptions 1-6: h Lipschitz in context (B'), u Lipschitz (B) and monotone in base rewards, ||x||_2=1 with symmetric entries and NTK H >= lambda_0 I, clustering assumption (delta_t decreasing, P_t non-decreasing), nonzero mean cluster contexts
proof takes delta_t = C_5/t and P_t = C_6 sqrt(t)
tuning: eta_1 = C_1 (T K m L + m lambda_1)^{-1}
C_2 L K <= lambda_1 <= 16 m 81 T^{-2 beta alpha+1} K^2 n^{2 L_m} / e_T^2
J = 2 log(sqrt(lambda_1/(TK))/(lambda_1 + C_3 T K L)) T K L/(C_1 lambda_1)

source.label: thm_1
source.quote: Supposing that Assumptions \ref{continuity_h}-\ref{ell0_assump} hold, let $\mathbf{h}=[h(\mathbf{x}^i)]_{i=1}^{TN}]$, and select the hyperparameters of the algorithm as follows ... Then if $m$ is chosen such that it satisfies Condition 1, the cumulative expected regret of NeUClust over $T$ rounds is bounded by $\mathcal{R}(T) = \widetilde{O}\left(\widetilde{d}\sqrt{T}\right)$

results.notes: d_eff is the NTK effective dimension. Regret is defined through expected super-arm rewards (pseudo-regret). The theorem calls it 'cumulative expected regret' but states no probability; the proof combines lemmas that each hold with probability 1-Delta (the explicit bound contains a -2 log Delta term), so I recorded it as high-probability. Canonical mapping: the paper's N (number of arms) is the canonical K, and the paper's K (super-arm size) is the canonical m. The explicit bound in the proof is linear in K (super-arm size) and depends on n^{L_m}, N and sqrt(d). The appendix 'Theorem 2' repeats this result.
